claim: The photographic damage that makes cel-era anime look old, added deliberately rather than inherited from a real camera. Halation and grain sell the age; the jitter and weave options sell it even harder but only once the clip moves.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: dust and scratches, damaged film, scratched print
halation, glowing highlight bloom, light bleed
paper texture, traditional media, textured overlay

review.issue: registration_jitter, telecine_wobble and gate_weave all carry empty clauses inside a renderable:true card, so they produce three byte-identical baseline panels sitting next to each other in the same card. The claim admits they only exist in motion, which is the right diagnosis but the wrong outcome.
review.fix: Give those three options an explicit per-option renderable:false (or move them into a separate motion-only variable marked renderable:false) so the card does not ship three duplicate stills. Keep film_grain, dust_scratches, halation and paper_texture, which do render. Also add a "none" baseline - as written every panel carries damage and there is nothing to compare against.
